meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll skip the pleasantries. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and why did I find out from my son's phone?
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. On what basis did you enter it?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing down November 2. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck" and can't place a paragraph, and you call that a finding? Show me the note you made that day.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
I'm writing that down. A student who changes his argument between an outline and a draft is revising, Hale. Put the outline and the essay in front of me, side by side.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's 4.4, and I want it in writing, Friday at 3 PM as you said. I still haven't seen the outline and the essay side by side, so I'm not agreeing to anything yet. Is the zero still showing in the gradebook tonight, and who else will be in that room Thursday?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook, the outline and the essay shown to me side by side, and the rewrite held privately with nothing on his file. I expect your written confirmation by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback; she agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook, the outline and essay shown to her, and a private rewrite with nothing on his record confirmed in writing. Your offer matches the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, but she never got to see any document, so she stopped short of accepting it.
What moved her: You offered the supervised rewrite with the replacement mark, nothing on his record, and a written confirmation by a set time, because that is exactly what procedure 4.4 says and it met her fallback demand.
What cost ground: You described the November 2 conversation and the outline that differs from the essay but never put a document in front of her, so she had nothing she could check, and you skipped her request to see them.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed away from that night, since you spoke of a conversation on November 2 and an outline from October 15, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the note you wrote on November 2, show it or read it out before moving to the outline, so each piece of evidence lands as something she can check.
